subproblem.title: Deformation theorem, scaled version (Simon 5.1/5.3)
subproblem.statement: For all m, ℓ ∈ ℕ with ℓ ≥ 1 there is C = C(m,ℓ) ∈ [0,∞) such that for every T ∈ D_{m+1}(ℝ^{m+1+ℓ}) with M(T) + M(∂T) < ∞ and every ρ > 0 there are β : 𝓛_{m+1}(ρ) → ℝ, Pc = Σ_F β_F[[F]] (IsLatticeChain ρ β Pc), R ∈ D_{m+2}(ℝ^{m+1+ℓ}) and S ∈ D_{m+1}(ℝ^{m+1+ℓ}) with T − Pc = ∂R + S, M(Pc) ≤ C M(T), M(∂Pc) ≤ C M(∂T), M(R) ≤ CρM(T), M(S) ≤ CρM(∂T), spt Pc ∪ spt R ⊆ {dist(·, spt T) < 2√(m+1+ℓ)ρ}, spt ∂Pc ∪ spt S ⊆ {dist(·, spt ∂T) < 2√(m+1+ℓ)ρ}; if T is integer multiplicity then every β_F ∈ ℤ and Pc, R are integer multiplicity, and if moreover ∂T is integer multiplicity then S is integer multiplicity.
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon, Ch. 6, §5 (pp. 158–168): statements 5.1 and 5.3, Lemma 5.4 with its printed proof, and the printed “Proof of the Deformation Theorem” (displays (1)–(38)); together with the tools it cites from §§2–4: products with [[(0,1)]] (2.17–2.21), push-forward and homotopy formula (2.23–2.29), 2.35–2.37, 3.2, 3.13, 4.5 and 4.10, and Ch. 2, 2.7–2.9. The printed proof is copied below in numbered form with the details needed for the exact Lean statement filled in. Errata applied: (i) the book's “n, k ∈ {1,2,…}”, “C = C(n,k)”, “L_{k−1}” mean n, ℓ ≥ 1, C(n,ℓ), L_{ℓ−1} (cf. the errata recorded in the docstring of `DeformationTheorem`); (ii) in 5.3 “P = Σ_{F∈𝓛_j(ρ)}” means F ∈ 𝓛_n(ρ), and “if ∂T is integer multiplicity then so is s” means S; (iii) the sign in (20) is corrected (homotopy formula 2.25 with f = id, g = ψ gives X − ψ_#X = −∂h_#([[(0,1)]]×X) − h_#([[(0,1)]]×∂X)); signs of R₁, S₁ are chosen accordingly; (iv) the printed bounds in (11)–(16) are stated as “≤ cM(T)”; the computations give the sharper ≤ cρM(T) (resp. cρ², cσ) used for the Cauchy property; (v) in (23) “<” is replaced by “≤” for the intermediate supports (the final strict bound < 2√(n+ℓ) follows since √n < √(n+ℓ)); (vi) in the selection of the good point a, the measure estimate (5) is replaced by the correct Fubini bound written in Step C2. (vii) The printed estimates (11)–(18) are applied to the pieces T_ρ − T_{ρ/2}, (∂T)_ρ − (∂T)_{ρ/2} for arbitrary ρ; since the Lipschitz push-forward 2.29 requires finite boundary mass, they are stated here only for differences between consecutive “good” radii σ_ν at which the slices of T and of ∂T have finite mass, and the uniform bounds (17)–(18) are obtained by telescoping. Details supplied beyond the printed text in A3 (behind the printed remark “Q, R₁ are integer multiplicity by (19), 4.4, 4.5 and 3.13”): (I) the limit passage identifying the Lipschitz push-forward 2.29 of an integer multiplicity current with the push-forward formula 3.6 fixes a compact target neighbourhood K of spt ω, shows that for all sufficiently small mollification parameters every contributing source point lies (H^k-a.e.) in the compact set g⁻¹(K) ∩ spt X, and dominates all integrands by one integrable function supported there before passing to the limit on each chart piece and summing over the pieces; (II) the identification with the push-forward supplied by the sibling theorem 3.9 compares the two representations of X by Radon–Nikodym uniqueness with respect to λ := H^k⌞(M ∪ M′). The representation X = τ(M′,θ′,ξ′) coming from `IsLipschitzPushforward` (through `IsRectifiableTriple`) has a merely positive, locally integrable real multiplicity θ′, which need not be integer valued or ≥ 1; σ-finiteness of λ is therefore proved from θ′ > 0 and the local integrability of θ′ alone (compact exhaustion K_j and the sets M′ ∩ K_j ∩ {θ′ ≥ 1/r}, each of H^k-measure ≤ r∫_{M′∩K_j}θ′ dH^k < ∞), and Radon–Nikodym uniqueness then gives H^k(M Δ M′) = 0, θ = θ′ and ξ = ξ′ H^k-a.e. on M ∩ M′.

Setting and notation. Book n := m + 1 ≥ 1, ℓ ≥ 1, d := n + ℓ, ambient ℝ^d = `Eucl (m+1+ℓ)`, all currents in U = ℝ^d (`univ`). C = [0,1]^d, q its centre; L_j the j-skeleton of the decomposition ⋃_{z∈ℤ^d}(z + C), 𝓛_j its closed j-faces, 𝓛_j(ρ) = {ρF}; S₁,…,S_N (N = C(d, n+1)) the (n+1)-dimensional coordinate subspaces, p_j the orthogonal projection onto S_j. For a ∈ B_{1/4}(q): L_{ℓ−1}(a) := a + L_{ℓ−1}, d_a(x) := dist(x, L_{ℓ−1}(a)) (1-Lipschitz), L_{ℓ−1}(a;ρ) := {d_a < ρ}. Since a has all coordinates in (1/4,3/4), every point of L_{ℓ−1}(a) has at least n+1 coordinates in a_i + ℤ and every point of L_n at least ℓ integer coordinates, so dist(L_{ℓ−1}(a), L_n) ≥ 1/4. Also (Simon (2)): L_{ℓ−1}(a) = ⋃_{j=1}^N ⋃_{z∈ℤ^d}(z + p_j⁻¹(p_j(a))), hence L_{ℓ−1}(a;ρ) = ⋃_j ⋃_{z∈ℤ^d∩S_j} p_j⁻¹(B_ρ(p_j(a)+z)) (balls in S_j). Conventions (stated here so that this proof is self-contained). For an ambient dimension D, e₁,…,e_D is the standard basis of ℝ^D, I(k,D) the set of strictly increasing multi-indices γ = (γ₁ < ⋯ < γ_k) in {1,…,D}, e_γ := (e_{γ₁},…,e_{γ_k}) and dx^γ := dx^{γ₁}∧⋯∧dx^{γ_k}. For a k-covector α (`Covector (Eucl D) k`), |α| := (Σ_γ α(e_γ)²)^{1/2} (`covectorEuclideanNorm`); for a k-form ω, ‖ω‖ := sup_x |ω(x)|; for a k-vector w (`NVector (Eucl D) k`, a linear functional on k-covectors), ⟨α, w⟩ := w(α), w^γ := w(dx^γ) and |w| := (Σ_γ (w^γ)²)^{1/2}; ‖A‖ is the operator norm of a linear map A. Coordinate fact: every k-covector satisfies α = Σ_γ α(e_γ)dx^γ (an alternating k-linear map is determined by its values on increasing tuples of basis vectors, and dx^γ(e_δ) = δ_{γδ}); hence w(α) = Σ_γ α(e_γ)w^γ and |w(α)| ≤ |α|·|w| (Cauchy–Schwarz). Push-forward of k-vectors: for a linear map A : ℝ^D → ℝ^{D′}, A_# = Λ_kA := `nVectorPushforward k A` is characterized by ⟨α, A_#w⟩ = ⟨A^#α, w⟩ with A^#α := α(A·,…,A·) (Simon 1.8–1.9); it is linear and A_#(simpleNVector τ) = simpleNVector(Aτ₁,…,Aτ_k) (Simon 1.10; SimonGMT `nVectorPushforward_simple`). Unit fact: if τ₁,…,τ_k ∈ ℝ^D are orthonormal then |simpleNVector τ| = 1, because its coordinates (simpleNVector τ)^γ = det(τ_i·e_{γ_j}) are the k×k minors of the D×k matrix with columns τ₁,…,τ_k and, by the Cauchy–Binet formula, Σ_γ det(τ_i·e_{γ_j})² = det(τ_i·τ_j) = 1; consequently, whenever `IsRectifiableTriple U k M θ ξ` holds, |ξ| = 1 H^k-a.e. on M (orientation clause). Mass M = `mass`, spt = `support`.

Part A — tools (Simon §§2–4, Ch. 2).

A1 (Representation, restriction; 2.7–2.9, 2.12). Every X ∈ D_k(ℝ^d) with locally finite mass is X(ω) = ∫⟨ω, X⃗⟩dμ_X with μ_X Radon, |X⃗| = 1 μ_X-a.e., μ_X(W) = M_W(X) for open W (vector Riesz theorem, Ch. 1, 4.14, applied to the ‖·‖-continuous extension of X to continuous compactly supported forms; mollification shows the sup over continuous and over smooth forms agree). Any `IsMeasureRepresentation` of X defines the same vector measure (both agree on continuous compactly supported forms). For Borel A, X⌞A(ω) := ∫_A⟨ω,X⃗⟩dμ_X is the unique S with `IsRestriction X A S`, and M_W(X⌞A) = μ_X(W ∩ A); spt X = spt μ_X; a test form vanishing on a neighbourhood of spt X is annihilated by X (partition of unity over the zero region); |X(ω)| ≤ M_W(X)‖ω‖ when tsupport ω ⊆ W; if M(X) = 0 then X = 0.

A2 (Products and push-forwards; 2.17–2.29). (a) For X ∈ D_k(ℝ^d) of locally finite mass, [[(0,1)]]×X ∈ D_{k+1}(ℝ × ℝ^d) is represented by e₁∧X⃗ and L¹⌞(0,1) × μ_X; ∂([[(0,1)]]×X) = {1}×X − {0}×X − [[(0,1)]]×∂X (2.19, 2.21, 2.22). (b) For C¹ (resp. smooth) f with f|spt X proper, f_#X(ω) := X(ζ f^#ω) (2.23, ζ ∈ C_c^∞ equal to 1 near spt X ∩ spt f^#ω), ∂f_# = f_#∂, and f_#X(ω) = ∫⟨ω(f(x)), Df(x)_#X⃗(x)⟩dμ_X (2.24(2)); hence M_W(f_#X) ≤ sup_{f⁻¹(W)∩spt X}‖Df‖^k·M_{f⁻¹(W)}(X), using |Λ_kA w| ≤ ‖A‖^k|w| (the singular values of Λ_kA are products of k singular values of A). (c) Homotopy formula (2.25): if h(0,·) = f, h(1,·) = g and h|[0,1]×spt X is proper, then g_#X − f_#X = ∂h_#([[(0,1)]]×X) + h_#([[(0,1)]]×∂X). (d) Affine homotopy estimate (2.27): for h(t,x) = f(x) + t(g(x) − f(x)), M_W(h_#([[(0,1)]]×X)) ≤ sup_{spt X∩W_h}|f−g|·sup_{spt X∩W_h}(‖Df‖+‖Dg‖)^k·M_{W_h}(X), W_h := pr(h⁻¹(W)). (e) Lemma 2.28–2.29: if M_W(X), M_W(∂X) < ∞ for all W and f is Lipschitz with f|spt X proper, then f_#X(ω) := lim_{ε↓0}(f_ε)_#X(ω) exists (f_ε = ϕ_ε*f mollified; by (c),(d) |(f_ε)_#X(ω) − (f_{ε′})_#X(ω)| ≤ C sup_{f⁻¹(K)∩spt X}|f_ε − f_{ε′}|(Lip f)^k (‖dω‖ + ‖ω‖)·(M(X)+M(∂X)) locally), spt f_#X ⊆ closure f(spt X), M_W(f_#X) ≤ (ess sup_{f⁻¹(W)}‖Df‖)^k M_{f⁻¹(W)}(X), ∂f_# = f_#∂, f_#X depends only on f on a neighbourhood of spt X, and (c),(d) remain valid for Lipschitz maps (pass to the limit ε ↓ 0). A locally Lipschitz map defined on an open set containing a neighbourhood of spt X on which it is Lipschitz is used through any Lipschitz extension (componentwise McShane, `LipschitzOnWith.extend_real`); the result does not depend on the extension. For k = 0 (X a signed Radon measure) f_#X(φ) := X(φ∘f) for continuous f with f|spt X proper; no boundary condition is needed.

A3 (Consistency for integer multiplicity currents; the step behind the printed remark “Q, R₁ are integer multiplicity by (19), 4.4, 4.5 and 3.13”). Let X ∈ D_k(ℝ^D) be integer multiplicity, X = τ(M,θ,ξ) with `IsRectifiableTriple univ k M θ ξ` (U = ℝ^D) and θ(x) ∈ {1,2,…} for x ∈ M (`IsIntegerMultiplicity X`), with locally finite boundary mass (no condition if k = 0), and let g : ℝ^D → ℝ^{D′} be Lipschitz, Λ := Lip(g), with g|spt X proper. Let L(x) := d^Mg_x∘π_{T_xM}, where T_xM is the weighted approximate tangent space of (M,θ) at x and d^Mg_x the tangential differential of Simon Ch. 3, §2 (both defined H^k-a.e. on M; ‖L(x)‖ ≤ Λ), and S(ω) := ∫_Mθ⟨ω(g(x)), L(x)_#ξ(x)⟩dH^k for ω ∈ D^k(ℝ^{D′}). Then (I) g_#X (A2(e)) equals S, and (II) g_#X is integer multiplicity. Part (I) is proved in steps (a)–(g); part (II) in steps (II.1)–(II.7), by identifying S with the integer multiplicity push-forward supplied by the sibling theorem `LipschitzPushforwardIntegerMultiplicity`.
Proof of (I): g_#X = S. Fix ω ∈ D^k(ℝ^{D′}) and let g_ε := ϕ_ε * g be the mollified maps of A2(e).
 (a) (A fixed compact target neighbourhood.) Let K₀ := tsupport ω and K := {y : dist(y, K₀) ≤ 1}, a compact set. Since |g_ε(x) − g(x)| ≤ ∫|g(x−z) − g(x)|ϕ_ε(z)dz ≤ Λε and g_ε is Λ-Lipschitz (so ‖Dg_ε‖ ≤ Λ everywhere), for 0 < ε ≤ ε₀ := 1/(1+Λ) we have: g_ε(x) ∈ K₀ ⇒ g(x) ∈ K. Hence for all such ε, ω(g_ε(x)) = 0 unless x ∈ g⁻¹(K), and likewise ω(g(x)) = 0 unless x ∈ g⁻¹(K).
 (b) (The contributing source points lie in one compact set.) K″ := g⁻¹(K) ∩ spt X is compact (properness of g|spt X). Moreover H^k(M ∖ spt X) = 0: the total variation measure of X is μ_X = θH^k⌞M (A1, as |ξ| = 1 H^k-a.e. on M by the unit fact of the Conventions), and μ_X(ℝ^D ∖ spt X) = 0 (A1: spt X = spt μ_X), so ∫_{M∖spt X}θ dH^k = 0 while θ ≥ 1 on M (θ is a positive integer on M, X being integer multiplicity; positivity of θ alone would suffice). Consequently, for 0 < ε ≤ ε₀, H^k-almost every x ∈ M at which ω(g_ε(x)) ≠ 0 or ω(g(x)) ≠ 0 lies in K″.
 (c) (Integrable dominator.) For 0 < ε ≤ ε₀ put F_ε(x) := θ(x)⟨ω(g_ε(x)), Dg_ε(x)_#ξ(x)⟩ and F(x) := θ(x)⟨ω(g(x)), L(x)_#ξ(x)⟩. Using |⟨α, A_#w⟩| ≤ |α|‖A‖^k|w| (A2(b)), |ξ| = 1 H^k-a.e. on M, ‖Dg_ε‖ ≤ Λ, ‖L(x)‖ ≤ Λ and (a)–(b): |F_ε(x)| ≤ G(x) and |F(x)| ≤ G(x) for H^k-a.e. x ∈ M, where G := ‖ω‖Λ^kθ1_{K″}. G is H^k⌞M-integrable because K″ is compact and θ is integrable on M ∩ K″ (`integrableOn` of the triple, U = ℝ^D). F_ε is H^k⌞M-measurable (g_ε is smooth, θ and ξ are measurable), and F is H^k⌞M-measurable: on each chart piece G_i of (e), F∘Φ_i is given by the formula of (f) below in terms of θ∘Φ_i, the measurable coefficient c and the minors of Du (Du is Borel, as an a.e. limit of difference quotients), and Φ_i⁻¹ maps H^k-null sets to L^k-null sets (Φ_i⁻¹ is the restriction of a 1-Lipschitz affine map). Hence F_ε and F are H^k⌞M-integrable.
 (d) (Smooth push-forwards.) g_ε|spt X is proper (g_ε⁻¹(K₁) ∩ spt X ⊆ g⁻¹({dist(·,K₁) ≤ Λε}) ∩ spt X), and by A2(b), (g_ε)_#X(ω) = X(ζg_ε^#ω) = ∫_Mθζ⟨ω(g_ε), Dg_ε_#ξ⟩dH^k, where ζ ∈ C_c^∞ equals 1 near spt X ∩ spt g_ε^#ω (duality 1.9: ⟨Dg_ε(x)^#ω(g_ε(x)), ξ(x)⟩ = ⟨ω(g_ε(x)), Dg_ε(x)_#ξ(x)⟩). At H^k-a.e. x ∈ M we have x ∈ spt X by (b), and either x ∈ spt g_ε^#ω (then ζ(x) = 1) or the integrand vanishes; so (g_ε)_#X(ω) = ∫_MF_ε dH^k.
 (e) (Chart pieces.) Write M = M₀ ∪ ⋃_{j≥1}M_j (disjoint, H^k-measurable), H^k(M₀) = 0, M_j ⊆ N_j embedded k-dimensional C¹ submanifolds (Simon Ch. 3, Lemma 1.2 and Remark 1.3, which use the C¹ approximation theorem Ch. 2, 1.5; embedded C¹ submanifolds are locally closed, hence Borel). Each point of N_j has a graph chart Φ : Ω → N_j, Ω ⊆ ℝ^k an open ball, Φ(w) = x₀ + Q(w, h(w)) with Q orthogonal and h C¹ with ‖Dh‖ ≤ 1 on Ω; then |DΦ(w)v| ≥ |v|, ‖DΦ‖ ≤ 2 and the Jacobian satisfies JΦ = det(DΦᵀDΦ)^{1/2} ≥ 1. By Lindelöf countably many such charts cover each N_j; disjointifying gives pairwise disjoint H^k-measurable sets G_i (i ∈ ℕ) with M ∖ M₀ = ⋃_iG_i and G_i ⊆ Φ_i(Ω_i) ∩ M_{j(i)}. By (c), F_ε and F are H^k⌞M-integrable, so by countable additivity (g_ε)_#X(ω) = Σ_ia_i(ε) and S(ω) = ∫_MF dH^k = Σ_ia_i, where a_i(ε) := ∫_{G_i}F_ε dH^k, a_i := ∫_{G_i}F dH^k; and |a_i(ε)|, |a_i| ≤ b_i := ∫_{G_i}G dH^k with Σ_ib_i = ∫_MG dH^k < ∞, for all 0 < ε ≤ ε₀.
 (f) (Convergence on one piece: weak continuity of minors.) Fix i; write Φ = Φ_i, Ω = Ω_i, N = N_{j(i)}, u_ε := g_ε∘Φ (C¹ on Ω, ‖Du_ε‖ ≤ 2Λ) and u := g∘Φ (Lipschitz on Ω; by Rademacher's theorem and the definition of d^Mg via C¹ charts, u is differentiable at Lᵏ-a.e. w ∈ Φ⁻¹(G_i) with Du(w) = d^Mg_{Φ(w)}∘DΦ(w) — only such w are used). Then |u_ε − u| ≤ Λε on Ω. For H^k-a.e. x = Φ(w) ∈ G_i, ξ(x) is a unit simple k-vector orienting T_xM = T_xN = DΦ(w)(ℝ^k) (orientation property of the triple, Ch. 3, Remark 1.5(2) and Remark 1.8(1) together with the Upper Density Theorem Ch. 1, 3.6, which identify the weighted tangent space of (M,θ) with T_xN at H^k-a.e. x ∈ M_j), so ξ(Φ(w)) = c(w)·∂₁Φ(w)∧⋯∧∂_kΦ(w) with c(w) := ⟨ξ(Φ(w)), ∂₁Φ∧⋯∧∂_kΦ⟩/|∂₁Φ∧⋯∧∂_kΦ|² measurable and |c(w)| = 1/JΦ(w) (|∂₁Φ∧⋯∧∂_kΦ| = JΦ). By the chain rule Dg_ε(Φ(w))∂_bΦ(w) = ∂_bu_ε(w), hence Dg_ε(x)_#ξ(x) = c(w)·∂₁u_ε(w)∧⋯∧∂_ku_ε(w), whose coordinates are the k×k minors M_γ(Du_ε(w)) (γ ∈ I(k,D′)); likewise L(x)_#ξ(x) = c(w)·∂₁u(w)∧⋯∧∂_ku(w) at a.e. w. By the area formula for the injective C¹ map Φ (change of variables, Simon Ch. 2, 3.4) and (a)–(b) (which allow inserting 1_{K″}), for 0 < ε ≤ ε₀:
 a_i(ε) = Σ_γ∫_Ωψ(w)·ω_γ(u_ε(w))·M_γ(Du_ε(w)) dw,  a_i = Σ_γ∫_Ωψ(w)·ω_γ(u(w))·M_γ(Du(w)) dw,
 where ω_γ := ω(e_γ) and ψ(w) := 1_{Φ⁻¹(G_i∩K″)}(w)·θ(Φ(w))·c(w)·JΦ(w). Here |ψ| = θ∘Φ·1_{Φ⁻¹(G_i∩K″)}, so ∫_Ω|ψ|dw ≤ ∫_{Φ⁻¹(G_i∩K″)}θ(Φ(w))JΦ(w)dw = ∫_{G_i∩K″}θ dH^k < ∞ (JΦ ≥ 1): ψ ∈ L¹(Ω).
 Weak continuity of minors. Claim: if v_ε, v : Ω → ℝ^{D′} are Lipschitz, sup_ε‖Dv_ε‖_∞ < ∞ and v_ε → v uniformly, then every r×r minor M(Dv_ε) (rows a₁,…,a_r, columns b₁,…,b_r) converges to M(Dv) weakly-* in L^∞(Ω), i.e. ∫ηM(Dv_ε) → ∫ηM(Dv) for every η ∈ L¹(Ω). Proof by induction on r.
